nodes.label: El-Messery Broiler Thermal Imaging Sample Grid
nodes.description: Research figure: a 5-column x 4-row panel grid (rows labelled A1-A5, B1-B5, C1-C5, D1-D5) of paired thermal-infrared and RGB images of broiler chickens. Row A shows whole-bird IR thermograms with spot temperatures (36.8, 35.8, 36.5, 29.1, 31.9 C) and timestamps; row B shows the corresponding visible-light photographs with coloured bounding-box ROIs drawn over the bird/body region; row C shows cropped ROI thermograms annotated with Avg/High/Low temperature statistics (e.g. Avg 31 C, High 34 C, Low 25.8 C); row D shows segmented/thresholded false-colour temperature maps with the same statistics. Demonstrates an ROI-based thermal measurement pipeline: detect bird in RGB, register the box onto the thermogram, crop, then compute regional surface-temperature statistics.
nodes.rationale: Paired RGB+IR acquisition with a bounding-box ROI is used because a whole-frame thermogram includes floor, litter and background heat that biases the bird's true surface temperature; restricting statistics to a detected ROI isolates the animal and makes Avg/High/Low temperature comparable across birds and sessions.

nodes.label: Thermal ROI Surface-Temperature Measurement
nodes.source_location: rows B-D of the panel grid
nodes.description: Method: draw a region of interest over the bird, crop the corresponding thermogram, and reduce it to Avg / High / Low temperature values plus a segmented false-colour map. Reported averages span roughly 29.6-39.8 C with highs to 40.9 C.
nodes.rationale: Scalar summary statistics per ROI make thermal state machine-comparable and enable thresholding for heat-stress classification without needing per-pixel calibration of the whole scene.

nodes.label: Broiler Surface Temperature Indicator
nodes.description: Body-surface temperature of broiler chickens measured non-invasively by infrared thermography and used as a physiological welfare / thermal-comfort indicator.
nodes.rationale: Surface temperature is preferred over cloacal or core temperature because it can be captured contactlessly at flock scale without handling stress that itself perturbs the measurement.
